ordered_diagnoses: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System

s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of neurological deficits with visual disturbances, headache, and fever in a patient with a history of autoimmune disease
salient_findings: T2 hyperintense lesions in the frontal, left parietal, and left occipital lobes with leptomeningeal enhancement on brain MRI
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showing elevated protein and white blood cells
Diffuse stenosis and beaded pattern of the anterior and middle cerebral arteries on cerebral angiography
key_facts: 41-year-old woman with a 3-year history of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis
History of skin sclerosis, Raynaud’s phenomenon, digital ulcers, facial telangiectasias, esophageal reflux, and interstitial lung disease
Positive antinuclear antibody titer with a nucleolar pattern
Negative anti-centromere antibody and anti-Scl-70 antibody
Admitted with fever over 38°C and headache
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis showed protein 161.6 mg/dL and white blood cells 459 /mm3
Brain MRI showed T2 hyperintense lesions in the frontal, left parietal, and left occipital lobes
Developed visual disturbances, headache, dizziness, fever, myalgia, polyarthralgia, and bilateral foot tingling
Neurologic examination revealed drowsiness, neck stiffness, symmetrical proximal and distal weakness, paresthesia in both feet, and brisk biceps reflexes
Emergent cerebral angiography revealed diffuse stenosis and a beaded pattern of the anterior and middle cerebral arteries

shortlist: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System

shortlist.label: Central Nervous System Vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of autoimmune disease and presents with subacute onset of neurological deficits, visual disturbances, and fever, which are consistent with CNS vasculitis

shortlist.label: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's cerebral angiography revealed diffuse stenosis and a beaded pattern of the anterior and middle cerebral arteries, which is consistent with primary angiitis of the CNS

shortlist.label: Susac's Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with visual disturbances, headache, and neurological deficits, which are consistent with Susac's syndrome, a rare autoimmune disorder that affects the brain and retina

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of autoimmune disease and presents with neurological deficits, fever, and headache, which are consistent with SLE

shortlist.label: Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presents with subacute onset of neurological deficits, visual disturbances, and fever, which are consistent with PCNSL, a rare type of lymphoma that affects the brain

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including visual disturbances, headache, dizziness, fever, myalgia, polyarthralgia, and bilateral foot tingling, along with the findings of T2 hyperintense lesions on brain MRI and diffuse stenosis and a beaded pattern of the anterior and middle cerebral arteries on cerebral angiography, are consistent with central nervous system vasculitis, which is a known complication of systemic sclerosis.

rejected.label: Primary Angiitis of the Central Nervous System
rejected.why: While the cerebral angiography findings could suggest primary angiitis, the patient's underlying systemic sclerosis and other systemic symptoms make CNS vasculitis a more likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Susac's Syndrome
rejected.why: Susac's syndrome typically presents with a triad of encephalopathy, branch retinal artery occlusions, and hearing loss, which are not all present in this case.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient's negative anti-Scl-70 antibody and lack of other specific lupus criteria make SLE less likely.

rejected.label: Primary Central Nervous System Lymphoma
rejected.why: The patient's cerebrospinal fluid analysis and brain MRI findings do not specifically suggest lymphoma, and the presence of systemic symptoms and underlying systemic sclerosis point towards a vasculitic process.
